ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE), as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulations of 1 February 2019 on RBE content, filing and access; Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and annual accounts; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF Circular 18/698; CSSF Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 on information accompanying transfers of funds. Access to the RBE is restricted to competent authorities and to AML/CFT obliged entities in the course of customer due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors / general meeting of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization with notarized attestation of corporate capacity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding screening of all shareholders, directors, managers and natural-person UBOs against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the Luxembourg high-risk third-country list published by the CSSF, and PEP databases covering foreign, domestic and international-organization PEPs; enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction nexus or unusual financing structure; source of wealth and source of funds documentation is mandatory for every UBO meeting the 25% threshold, with annual refresh and event-triggered re-screening; suspicious transaction reports are filed with the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de renseignement financier - CRF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessible via lbr.lu / rcs.lu and the e-Justice / guichet.lu filing portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name of the SARL must be registered in Latin script; Luxembourg law does not impose a single official language for the name, but the RCS working language is French and filings are made in French; non-Latin script names must include a certified Latin-script transliteration in the notarial deed; the name must be distinguishable from existing registered names, must not mislead the public as to the object or legal form, and must not infringe third-party trade names or trademarks.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fonds / Fund / Fonds du marché monétaire / Money Market Fund
Société d'investissement / Investment Company / SICAV / SIF / RAIF
État / State / Ministère / Ministry / National / Nation
Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Commerce
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Agence de notation / Rating Agency
Union Européenne / European Union and EU-related emblems and words
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RCS does not operate an indefinite shelf-reservation system; the 30-day benchmark is the period during which the notary keeps a pre-cleared name available for execution of the incorporation deed. If the RCS rejects the proposed name on grounds of confusion, misleading character, prohibited token or insufficient distinguishability, counsel must submit a reasoned rectification through the LBR/guichet.lu portal within 15 calendar days or propose an amended name; the incorporator may file an administrative appeal (recours gracieux) with the competent administration or the Minister of Justice within one month of the rejection notice, followed by judicial appeal (recours en annulation) before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within three months of the final administrative decision; no provisional corporate registration is available while an appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the proposed trade-finance and factoring entity: the CSSF AML/CFT supervision, the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, and the RBE framework require a genuine physical establishment in Luxembourg where the statutory seat, corporate books, accounting records, KYC/AML files, the AML compliance officer function and senior management are located. A serviced or virtual office may be used only as an ancillary administrative address; a licensed domiciliation agent may provide a registered office for a non-regulated holding entity, but this arrangement is not acceptable for a company carrying out accounts-receivable factoring over SWIFT and escrow rails without prior CSSF comfort.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High-frequency risk: estimated 60-80% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by the CSSF, the CRF or the Luxembourg police AML unit within the first 18-24 months of operation, given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML risk tier assigned to cross-border trade supply-chain factoring and the reliance on cross-border payment rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended by the Law of 10 August 2016 and the Law of 23 September 2020; SARL provisions at Articles 710-1 to 710-23 (Book VII); Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and annual accounts; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector for factoring licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés de Luxembourg (RCS), administered through the eJustice portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif) executed before a Luxembourg notary and filed with the RCS; publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) in the name of the SARL in formation with a Luxembourg credit institution or the Caisse de Consignation; a bank attestation de blocage certifying the deposit must be delivered to the notary before signature of the deed of incorporation, and the funds remain blocked until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founders' subscription of 12,000 fully paid-up shares of one euro each is ratified and allocated in accordance with the deed of incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [registered address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed Gérant (Manager) and [Name] is appointed Compliance Officer, each with authority to file documents with the Luxembourg Business Registers and the RCS, to open bank accounts, and to pursue the CSSF professional-of-the-financial-sector licence for factoring. RESOLVED FINALLY, that the Manager may engage notaries, counsel and auditors and take all steps necessary to complete statutory formation, RBE filing, and licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) eJustice flagship portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed names through the eJustice portal; the RCS verifies availability and checks for confusing similarity against existing registrations and protected marks. The chosen name must lawfully include the suffix 'société à responsabilité limitée' or 'SARL'. Upon approval the name is reserved for the company in formation pending registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusing similarity, file an alternative name within 5 working days or appeal the refusal to the RCS; adjust the corporate purpose to remove terms reserved for licensed financial institutions if queried.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Escrow Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) or Caisse de Consignation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or the founders open a blocked escrow account in the name of the SARL in formation and transfer at least EUR 12,000. The bank issues a blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) identifying the subscribers, the account holder, and the blocked amount. Subscription lists allocating shares to each founder are executed in line with the draft articles.
required_dossiers: Identification and residency evidence of subscribers
Bank KYC forms and beneficial ownership questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises enhanced due diligence queries, provide a source-of-wealth file and corporate reference letters; if the blocking certificate contains errors, the bank must issue a rectified certificate; the notary cannot proceed until a compliant certificate is produced.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) appointed by the Ministère de la Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founders appear in person or by notarised power of attorney before the notary. The notary verifies the legality of the articles, the adequacy of the capital deposit, and the identities of the signatories, reads the deed, and authenticates it. The notary thereafter files the deed with the RCS and arranges publication in the RESA.
required_dossiers: Valid passports of founders and managers
Written acceptance of office by each manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects, a supplemental rectificatif deed is signed; if a founder is absent, a duly notarised power of attorney (procuration) is obtained; material deviations require a redraft of the articles before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS Luxembourg / Luxembourg Business Registers (eJustice portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the incorporation deed with the RCS within one month of signature and pays the statutory filing fee. The RCS assigns a registration number (numéro d'immatriculation) and the deed becomes enforceable against third parties upon registration and publication in the RESA. The legal existence of the SARL is perfected as of registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a demande de complément, cure the omission within 15 days via the eJustice file; if the corporate purpose includes regulated factoring activity, confirm that the CSSF authorisation application is pending and that the activity will not commence before licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), managed by the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the declaration of ultimate beneficial owners within one month of RCS registration. Identify all natural persons owning or controlling more than 25% of shares, voting rights, or other control. If no natural person is identified, a declaration of non-identification must be filed listing senior managing officials.
required_dossiers: Evidence of percentage of ownership or control
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE filing is queried, file a corrective declaration with a complete ownership chain; if control is indirect, add the intermediate entity documentation; ensure consistency with the CSSF AML file and the bank KYC record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, Social Security and Financial-Sector Licensing Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit tax registration forms to the ACD for corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) and net wealth tax (IFF); register with the AEDT for Luxembourg VAT; register as an employer with the CCSS. In parallel, file the CSSF application for a professional-of-the-financial-sector licence (PFS) authorising factoring under the Law of 5 April 1993, supported by an operational business plan and AML/CYP compliance programme.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and deed of incorporation
Articles of association and manager list
CSSF PFS licence application file with business plan and AML-CFT compliance manual
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resubmit corrected forms to the competent administrations; if the CSSF requests additional information, respond within the stated deadline of one month; if the application is incomplete, withdraw and refile with a complete business plan, projected financial statements, outsourcing description, and fit-and-proper declarations of managers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agrément en qualité de professionnel du secteur financier (PFS) – autorisation d'exercer l'activité d'affacturage (Authorization as a Professional of the Financial Sector for Factoring Activities under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the Financial Sector)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – simple declaration (registration) for office-only financial services premises; no full EIA report required as the activity involves no manufacturing, no combustion plant, and no classified Annex I/II project under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: no industrial effluent; sanitary discharges only, connected to municipal sewer under communal by-laws and the Law of 19 December 2008 on water management, with no process water. Emissions: VOC and dust screening levels below 0.5 tonnes per annum given dry-office operations; no IPPC/IED permit required. Waste: compliance with the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management and the Law of 21 April 2017 on extended producer responsibility, including mandatory segregation of paper, IT equipment, and electrical waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety conformity certificate from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) verifying evacuation routes, fire-extinguishing equipment, and smoke-detection installations; structural and electrical safety inspections issued by an accredited bureau de contrôle; workplace clearance obtained from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering ventilation, workstation ergonomics, electrical safety, hygiene, and first-aid equipment; occupational accident insurance coverage registered with the CCSS.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.aml_ctf_regime_note: The entity is classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced and must comply with the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended, including customer due diligence, beneficial ownership verification, transaction monitoring, and the designation of an AML compliance officer; CSSF registration complies with CSSF Regulation No 20-07.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; portal: https://guichet.lu (MyGuichet e-filing)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SARL must be incorporated and registered in the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS). Upon RCS registration, the ACD assigns a direct tax matricule number (numéro d'identification). To charge VAT or claim input VAT, a separate VAT identification number (TVA number) must be obtained from the AEDT using the VAT registration declaration Form 480/A before commencing taxable activities. Foreign entities without a Luxembourg establishment may apply for direct VAT registration through a Luxembourg tax representative. The statutory corporate TIN is the RCS matricule, complemented by the TVA number for indirect tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg tax law; a resident SARL is treated as a non-transparent, entity-level taxable corporation. Statutory elections available: (1) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) election for corporate income tax and municipal business tax among qualifying 95%-owned resident group companies; (2) VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) allowing multiple taxable persons to be treated as a single taxable person; (3) participation exemption election for qualifying dividends and capital gains. Hybrid mismatch rules are mandatorily applied under EU ATAD and do not require a taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) under the Luxembourg Loi TVA transposing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For Luxembourg-established small taxpayers: annual turnover threshold of EUR 35,000 for the small enterprise exemption. For foreign or non-resident entities, no registration threshold applies; VAT registration is mandatory before effecting any taxable supply in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing applies only to B2G transactions via the PEPPOL e-delivery network. There is no real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance requirement, or digital stamping for B2B or B2C invoices. VAT returns and EU recapitulative statements are filed electronically through MyGuichet with the AEDT; no continuous transaction control regime is currently in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero rating requires proof of physical export outside the EU, evidenced by customs export declaration and transport documents, or an intra-Community supply to an EU VAT-registered customer whose VAT ID is confirmed in VIES. Services: a zero-rate or outside-scope treatment applies if the place of supply under the B2B reverse-charge rules is outside Luxembourg or outside the EU. Factoring and accounts-receivable financing is VAT-exempt under Article 44 Loi TVA; when provided to a non-Luxembourg business, the place of supply is the customer's country, so no Luxembourg VAT falls due and input VAT (if any) is recovered via the periodic VAT return.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or erroneous zero-rating claims are subject to AEDT audit verification, retrospective clawback of VAT, reversal of input VAT recovery, and statutory interest on under-declared tax. Administrative fines up to EUR 10,000 (or up to EUR 100,000 in aggravated fraud cases) may be imposed; criminal liability, including imprisonment, applies under Article 211 Loi TVA. Directors, officers, and tax representatives may be held jointly and severally liable for the resulting VAT and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), jointly with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking and financial prudential supervision, and the Ministry of Finance for financial legislation
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Luxembourg applies the EU Treaty freedoms and implements the Law of 12 July 2017 on the obligation to collect balance of payments information; there are no exchange controls, no prior authorisation requirements for payments, and no restrictions on dividend or profit remittance beyond standard corporate law distribution tests and beneficial ownership disclosure requirements under the Law of 1 August 2019 on the professional activities of the financial sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation or surrender of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may hold foreign currency accounts domestically or abroad, subject only to the EU Balance of Payments reporting thresholds under CSSF circulars and BCL statistical reporting obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. An EU/EEA e-money institution passported into Luxembourg may provide payment accounts and transaction processing, but such EMI accounts are generally not suitable for capital escrow or factoring settlement because they do not offer credit facilities, commercial letters of credit, or segregated account features that full credit institutions provide. Additionally, Luxembourg financial sector regulation requires factoring activities to be conducted through robust banking channels, and credit institution underwriting standards often treat EMI accounts as higher risk due to their limited transparency and lack of direct supervisory coverage in Luxembourg.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally expected for legal representatives and ultimate beneficial owners during onboarding. Luxembourg banks apply the AML/CFT framework of the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF regulations as part of the national regime; while some banks allow remote video identification for natural persons, corporate account opening involving trade finance and an escrow account almost always requires an in-person board or KYC interview at the bank's premises or with a notarised legalisation of corporate documents. For a SARL with non-EU shareholders, the notarial deed of incorporation and the beneficial owner registration extract from the RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) must be produced, and authorised signatories may be required to appear.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) chain spanning multiple jurisdictions with nominee shareholders or layered special purpose vehicles, creating opacity of control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete RBE extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners; notarised share transfer deeds; certified copies of constitutional documents; organisational chart showing direct and indirect shareholding; declarations of beneficial ownership from each intermediary jurisdiction; passport copies and proof of residence for all UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High aggregate turnover of the factoring vehicle relative to stated paid-in capital, raising suspicion of unlicensed lending or money service business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements (at least two years); legally binding factoring master agreement and underlying trade invoices; external audit confirmation of the client receivables portfolio; transactional forecast model; VAT and corporate tax registrations evidencing the professed commercial activity; licences or exemption confirmations from the CSSF for the ISIC 6492 factoring activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border transaction counterparties domiciled in sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions on the FATF grey list, triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results from a reputable list; trade compliance letters; contracts incorporating ICC Incoterms 2020; bank reference letters for counterparties; shipping and logistics documentation; end-beneficiary declarations confirmed through a sworn statement and supporting certificates of origin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status of any director or UBO.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP screening system output with scoring; written explanation of the source of funds and source of wealth; notarised bank or tax statements covering the last 12 months; confirmation of low-risk government position with no involvement in procurement; independent legal opinion on full compliance with the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF AML/CFT requirements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity or shareholder loan injections, wire transfers should be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 with purpose codes B030 (equity capital) or S130 (shareholder loans), clearly referencing the SARL's name and the capital escrow account. Prior to execution, the bank requires a board resolution confirming the injection, a certificate of payment for share capital or a notarised shareholder loan agreement, and evidence of source funds. The CSSF balance of payments report must classify the transaction as direct investment; no prior approval is required, but the payment reason must be accurately encoded to support the treasury record.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Distributions to sellers in a supply chain factoring programme are effected by SEPA Credit Transfer in euro (SEPA CT) or by SWIFT MT103 for cross-border currency. For each disbursement, banks require a counterparty instruction, a commercial invoice, and a signed assignment or purchase-to-discount agreement. For large trade settlements, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (UCP 600) may be utilised through the confirming bank; standard clearing rails include SWIFT MT103/202, TARGET2 for critical euro settlement, and CLS for FX-linked payments. All outbound payments must be tagged with appropriate purpose codes and recorded under the entity's factoring receivable ledgers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forward contracts for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and other convertible currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to convertibility restrictions
Cross-currency interest rate swaps documented under ISDA with EMIR compliance
Currency swaps for liquidity management and cross-currency funding alignment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS file confirmation (confirmation annuelle du dossier RCS) — annual re-certification of registered corporate data and shareholding details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Trade and Companies Register (RCS / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month following the annual anniversary of the date of RCS registration of the SARL (each registration year; non-calendar anniversary rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted confirmation triggers RCS default proceedings, escalating administrative fines and additional publication costs; repeated non-renewal over successive annual anniversaries is a ground for administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) initiated by the Ministère Public, followed by compulsory liquidation and potential joint liability of the gérants.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts package (comptes annuels): balance sheet, profit-and-loss account and annex (bilan, compte de profits et pertes, annexe) in Luxembourg GAAP with notes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the eCDF electronic filing platform; copies required for the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) as supervising authority of the licensed factoring/PSF entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven (7) months following the balance-sheet date (financial year-end); for a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is 31 July of the following year; first accounts due for the first closed financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing within the legal deadline exposes the SARL and its gérants to (i) an administrative fine imposed by the RCS registrar (up to EUR 1,250, approx. USD 1,360), (ii) a peremptory court order obtained by the Ministère Public under threat of astreinte (penalty payment), (iii) CSSF supervisory measures for the regulated factoring business, including administrative pecuniary sanctions, and (iv) in unresolved cases, administrative strike-off and disqualification of the managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-ownership (UBO) data certification tied to the RCS annual confirmation; RBE registers of beneficial owners update request for any movement in the prior year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs); AML/CFT supervisor retained for the licensed PSP-Factoring activity: CSSF
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: RBE updates must be filed within one (1) month of any qualifying change in beneficial ownership (shareholding transfer thresholds of 25%, 50%, 75% and 100%); the annual RCS file confirmation concurrently certifies the accuracy of all UBO data as at the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The RBE Law of 13 January 2019 penalizes knowing failure to file or false UBO declarations with criminal fines for the SARL of up to EUR 1,250,000 (approx. USD 1,362,500) and imprisonment of up to six (6) months for responsible natural persons; CSSF may impose additional AML/CFT administrative pecuniary penalties, and the RCS may refuse the annual confirmation, escalating toward strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual CSSF supervisory filing for the licensed trade-factoring financial professional (PSF): audited financial statements, capital-adequacy/eligibility statement, AML/CFT compliance pack and annual clearance of UBO/regulatory files
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) — Prudential Supervision and AML/CFT Supervision Departments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months after the financial year-end (audited accounts and external auditor report), and no later than the CSSF annual AML/CFT data-collection calendar (including the AML factual report cycle); exact submission dates are set by CSSF circulars applicable to PSPs and professional factoring entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, inaccurate or omitted CSSF filings constitute a breach of the Luxembourg Financial Sector Law of 5 April 1993 and CSSF Circular 12/552; the CSSF may impose administrative fines, restrict or revoke the factoring authorization, require immediate remediation and capital add-ons, and refer material breaches to the criminal authorities; continuing non-compliance also undermines the RCS annual confirmation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint an approved independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) if, on the balance-sheet date and for two consecutive financial years, it exceeds at least two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million (approx. USD 4.8 million), net turnover EUR 8.8 million (approx. USD 9.6 million), average workforce 50 employees. Independently of size, the audit is mandatory for this entity because ISIC 6492 factoring is carried on under a CSSF license (Law of 5 April 1993 and CSSF Circular 12/552), and the CSSF always requires an annual statutory audit of licensed financial professionals of the factoring/PSF type.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 (annual accounts of undertakings), as amended by the Law of 23 September 2020, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; the SARL must use the BTS balance-sheet architecture in the eCDF filing scheme. IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for voluntary application on the statutory accounts but Luxembourg GAAP remains the default local statutory basis. Luxembourg Commercial Code generally prescribes a ten (10) year books-and-records preservation period; this compliance data model applies a standardized retention baseline of seven (7) years, which should be overridden by the local ten-year floor on site.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg imposes an event-driven, not calendar-annual, UBO declaration duty: any transfer or change in beneficial ownership (direct or indirect shareholding triggers at 25%, 50%, 75% and 100%) must be filed with the RBE within one month of the change, together with all supporting identification documents. The annual RCS file confirmation serves as the annual accuracy re-certification of UBO entries as at each registration anniversary. For the licensed factoring entity, the CSSF additionally requires a documented annual AML/KYB review, an updated internal beneficial-ownership register available on site, and the filing of the AML factual return with the RBE/CSSF per the relevant circulars; transfer of a controlled SARL shareholding above 25% therefore requires (i) transfer deed, (ii) update of the register of members, (iii) RBE filing within one month, and (iv) capture in the next annual RCS confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% CIT plus 7% unemployment-fund surcharge on CIT = 18.19%; for Luxembourg City, municipal business tax (ICC) at 6.75% produces an aggregate statutory headline rate of 24.94% for fiscal year 2024/2025.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box: 80% exemption on qualifying IP income (Art. 50bis LIR, nexus approach); participation exemption: 100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (Art. 166 LIR); deductible bad-debt provisioning on factored receivables within commercial prudence limits; no notional interest deduction for new financing as from 2021.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carry-forward; no carry-back permitted). Recapture risk under Art. 114bis LIR when a legal entity is acquired or its activity changes and the losses were sustained in the 5 preceding years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 - Declaration for Corporate Income Tax (IRC) and Municipal Business Tax (ICC); e-filing through MyGuichet.lu via an accredited tax adviser.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year SARL the deadline is 30 June of the following year, automatically extended to 31 December when filed through a certified registered tax adviser.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity name, RCS registration number, LEI, registered office, tax year opening and closing dates, legal form.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident factoring company with a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE): identify the PE, local registered agent and AED registration number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss per the statutory commercial balance sheet and profit-and-loss account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach PE-only financial statements reflecting the factoring business attributable to the Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses: unsubstantiated factoring discount charges, fines, excessive director fees, non-documented related-party payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers must document all intra-group factoring fee and discount allocations to Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of exempt income: qualifying participation-exemption dividends, IP Box relief, tax losses brought forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only to the extent the PE can evidence shareholding, holding period and substance conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of taxable income; application of 17% CIT, 7% employment-fund surcharge and ICC at the municipal coefficient.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same computation for the PE; request treaty MAP relief only if double taxation is not otherwise relieved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance CIT/ICC payments made during the year, withholding tax credits, final tax due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must attach evidence of advance payments made through the local AED account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Integrated net wealth tax declaration, Country-by-Country notification, transfer pricing documentation index.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the CbC notification and TP file if the group revenue or related-party threshold is exceeded.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers an estimated assessment (taxation d'office) and an administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 (Art. 174 StAnpG); late-payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month; fraudulent filing is prosecuted under Art. 178 StAnpG with imprisonment up to 5 years and/or fines.
